title: Final Capstone Report
goal: Design a scalable training program that closes the gap between academic bench-science training and the systems-level skills ExFAB's automated biofoundry requires.
description: A workforce training blueprint that closes the automation skills gap at UCSB's ExFAB biofoundry.
longWriteup:
CNSI's ExFAB biofoundry at UC Santa Barbara was scaling its automated, AI-integrated research capacity faster than the talent market could supply qualified operators. New graduates arrived fluent in manual bench science but unable to reason across the workflow orchestration, LIMS environments, and cross-instrument troubleshooting that modern biofoundries demand — a gap employers described less as a knowledge deficit than a failure to "think in systems rather than procedures."

As part of a six-person MTM consulting team, I helped lead and synthesize more than 60 semi-structured interviews with professionals across biopharma, synthetic biology, agtech, and clinical research to characterize the gap and identify the competencies that actually predicted performance. We translated those findings into an operational blueprint: a two-week, part-time bootcamp for 20–40 person cohorts, built around ExFAB's existing instrument suite and delivered through a blended dry-studio and wet-lab rotation model.

The design was deliberately constrained to require zero new full-time hires, no capital expenditure, and no facility modification, preserving ExFAB's research-first mission while making the program scalable. Financial modeling projected a $395,000 net annual contribution starting in Year 2, with the $86,450 setup investment fully recovered within the first cohort cycle.

title: Student Affiliate Program Proposal
goal: Design a student affiliate program that turns peer trust into adoption of the docusrch research platform on college campuses.
description: Peer-led affiliate program strategy to drive student adoption of a research platform.
longWriteup:
Docusrch, an AI-powered research and document analysis tool, needed a way to build credibility and adoption among college students — a segment that overwhelmingly discovers and adopts new tools through peers rather than ads. As part of UCSB's American Marketing Association, I led the research and strategy behind a proposed student affiliate program.

I grounded the proposal in primary research, surveying 93 UCSB students on how they discover and adopt academic tools. The data showed word of mouth (34%) and in-person conversation (41%) as the dominant channels, with social media as a secondary, more passive driver — findings that reshaped the program away from a typical influencer-affiliate model.

Based on those insights, I designed three distinct affiliate tracks — Knowledge Pioneers, deepsrch Creators, and Papertrail — each targeting a different type of student influence, from in-person research-lab integration to social content creation. For Knowledge Pioneers, I built out the full model: recruitment criteria, application and interview process, and an incentive structure (premium access, beta features, LinkedIn recognition, a public "Hall of Excellence") designed to reward sustained engagement over one-off referrals.

The proposal gave Docusrch a research-backed, ready-to-implement framework for turning students into credible brand advocates, prioritizing trust-building channels over paid or influencer-driven acquisition.

title: AMA Adobe Express Case
goal: Increase brand awareness of Adobe Express among college students and convert free-plan users into paid subscribers.
description: Student-led strategic marketing plan to grow Adobe Express adoption among college students.
longWriteup:
Situation: Adobe Express, Adobe's design and content-creation platform, had far lower brand recognition among college students than flagship products like Photoshop and Illustrator, despite offering a free university-email plan meant to build habitual use before graduation.

Task: As a team leader on a student consulting project for the American Marketing Association, I helped guide a cross-functional team through primary and secondary research to diagnose why student awareness and paid conversion lagged, then build a marketing plan to close that gap.

Action: The team ran industry, competitor, and PESTLE/SWOT analysis alongside primary consumer research to map student attitudes toward Adobe Express versus competing tools. From those insights, we designed a multi-channel campaign mix — a merchandise design competition, a campus influencer program, "Success with Express" hands-on workshops, and e-booth pop-ups — each paired with tactics and success metrics tied to awareness and free-to-paid conversion.

Result: The plan gave Adobe Express a research-backed, ready-to-execute roadmap for reaching college students, with campaign concepts, budgets, and measurement criteria organized for direct handoff to the client.

title: SeaVees Student Ambassadorship Proposal
goal: Pitch SeaVees on a college brand ambassador program that turns UCSB students into peer-to-peer marketers.
description: Ambassador program proposal for SeaVees, built for UCSB's American Marketing Association chapter.
longWriteup:
SeaVees wanted a way to reach Gen-Z college shoppers without relying on paid influencer spend. As part of UCSB's American Marketing Association, I helped build the case for a student ambassadorship program and present it as a formal proposal to the brand.

The report grounds the pitch in research: citing that referred customers carry 16% higher average value, that 70% of students act on ambassador content, and original AMA survey data showing 65% of respondents discover brands through word of mouth. I used UCSB's specific profile, second-hand shopping culture, beach proximity, its ranking as a top eco-conscious campus, and a downtown SeaVees store near campus, to argue why this school was the right pilot site.

The proposal outlines three distinct ambassador tracks ("Seekers," "Sole Crew," and "Thriftee") so the program could serve different content and community goals while staying replicable for a rollout to other campuses, along with implementation steps, promotion tactics, and measurement criteria.

The deliverable is a full ambassadorship proposal report that translates market research and audience analysis into a structured, pitch-ready program brief.

title: Predictive A&R Model: Cutting Spotify Marketing Waste
goal: Build a predictive screening model that filters low-potential tracks before marketing spend is committed, replacing artist-fame gut calls with an audio-feature-based signal.
description: Random forest model flags likely flops pre-release, saving Spotify an est. $14.37M/year in A&R marketing spend.
longWriteup:
Situation: Record labels commit full promotional budgets (roughly $50K per track) at the moment of release, with no signal for which songs will actually perform. Teams lean on artist fame as a proxy for quality, which reinforces existing stars and leaves genuine breakout tracks under-marketed. In the team's dataset of Spotify releases, the top 10 songs generated over $5.9M in streaming revenue while the bottom 10 earned almost nothing.

Task: As part of a six-person team in UCSB's MTM program, I worked on framing and communicating a predictive A&R screening tool for a fictional Spotify intelligence division — translating a random forest classification model into a business case and executive narrative a label decision-maker would actually act on.

Action: The team trained a random forest classifier on 550K Spotify tracks, controlling for artist popularity so the model reads audio features (loudness and acousticness emerged as the strongest flop predictors) rather than name recognition. Output was scoped into three tiers — Flop, Moderate, Hit — each mapped to a clear action: withhold marketing, route to human A&R review, or approve the $50K spend. I helped shape the executive summary and business-problem framing, translating model output into a bottom-line-up-front pitch built around dollars saved rather than model mechanics.

Result: Applied to a 1,000-release slate, the model filters out the bottom 33.1% before human review — removing 333 predicted failures and avoiding an estimated $16.65M in annual marketing spend, netting a projected $14.37M in business value after leakage and operating costs.

title: New Venture Competition Application
goal: Build the market validation and brand positioning case for a natural-fiber certification platform to win a university new venture competition.
description: Positioning, market validation, and competitive strategy for a natural-fiber clothing certification startup.
longWriteup:
Situation: Three UCSB Technology Management classmates and a software engineer wanted to enter a New Venture Competition with Loomi, a platform certifying and surfacing ethically sourced, natural-fiber clothing in a market where 60% of garments are synthetic and greenwashing is rampant.

Task: As the team member driving positioning and messaging, I needed to translate 30+ customer interviews into a clear problem statement, define the target customer and value proposition, and differentiate Loomi against direct competitors like Good On You and WorldChangerCo in a written application judges would use to decide funding.

Action: I helped structure the elevator pitch around a concrete health and trust concern (microplastic exposure from synthetic fabrics) validated by direct customer quotes, defined the ideal customer profile (health-conscious women 20-35 already shopping natural fiber), and wrote the three-point value proposition around fiber verification, ethical-sourcing research, and anti-greenwashing guarantees. I also wrote the competitive differentiation section, pinpointing exactly where rival platforms fall short at the product level.

Result: The application presented a coherent, evidence-backed brand story built from primary research rather than assumptions, giving the team a credible case for funding and a repeatable messaging framework (the "Fabric Facts" panel concept) the team carried into product design.

title: Docusrch Student Affiliate Program Proposal
goal: Pitch a peer-driven affiliate strategy to grow student awareness and adoption of docu srch.
description: Proposal for a three-track student affiliate program to drive campus awareness of an AI research tool.
longWriteup:
Docu srch, an AI-powered research tool that helps students and professionals extract insights from complex documents, needed a low-cost way to build brand awareness among college students, its primary user base.

I was asked to design an affiliate marketing proposal that would use peer influence and campus networks to drive trial and word-of-mouth adoption, grounded in survey insights on student research habits and platform behavior.

The proposal introduced three affiliate tracks — Knowledge Pioneers, deep srch Creators, and PaperTrail — each built around a different student persona, and paired them with a social content plan, implementation timeline, and rollout milestones.

The deck was presented to stakeholders as a ready-to-execute go-to-market plan, outlining the content calendar and next steps for recruiting and onboarding the first cohort of student affiliates.

title: Art Careers in the Heart of Los Angeles
goal: Give prospective students and readers a firsthand, relatable look at career paths in arts administration through an intern's museum visit.
description: Blog post for AD&A recapping an intern museum tour, framing real arts-career paths for prospective students.
longWriteup:
Written during Miguel's communications internship with AD&A, this post was part of the organization's public blog, aimed at giving prospective students and community members a behind-the-scenes look at what a career in the arts can actually involve.

Rather than a generic event recap, the piece uses a first-person tour of two major Downtown LA institutions, The Broad and a neighboring museum, as a narrative frame to walk readers through specific roles and departments within museum and arts administration.

The post ran as part of AD&A's ongoing content library, supporting the organization's efforts to recruit future interns and position itself as a resource for students exploring careers in the arts.

title: The AD&A Internship Experience
goal: Give prospective student applicants an authentic look at the internship program to build interest and drive future applications.
description: First-person blog post for the museum promoting its student internship program.
longWriteup:
Written while serving as Communications Intern at the AD&A Museum (UC Santa Barbara's Art, Design & Architecture Museum), this post was published on the museum's official blog to put a real voice behind the internship program rather than a generic recruiting blurb.

The piece frames the internship as more than gallery upkeep, positioning it as a professional launchpad for students headed into art and museum careers. Writing from the intern's own perspective let the museum speak credibly to prospective applicants — students trust a peer account more than a program description.

As a work sample, it shows the ability to write for a specific institutional voice and audience: warm and personal enough to resonate with students, polished enough to represent the museum publicly.

title: Summer Courses Enrollment Reminder Post
goal: Prompt existing users to open the app and browse newly added summer courses before enrollment windows closed.
description: Social reminder post driving app engagement around College Sauce's new summer course listings.
longWriteup:
College Sauce, a course-discovery app for college students, had just added summer course listings but needed a lightweight way to resurface the feature to users who might not check the app daily.

The task was to write and design a single reminder post that would catch attention in a crowded feed, communicate the update in one glance, and push users back into the app with minimal friction.

I wrote punchy, direct copy built around a clear "now available" hook, paired it with bold on-brand type treatment, and kept the call-to-action simple and singular so there was no ambiguity about the next step.

The post gave College Sauce a reusable template for feature-reminder content — a fast, low-lift way to re-engage users any time new courses or listings go live, without needing a full campaign each time.

title: Referral Leaderboard Launch
goal: Drive new user acquisition for College Sauce by gamifying referrals through a points-based leaderboard contest with tiered prizes.
description: Instagram carousel launching a referral leaderboard contest to drive app signups and engagement.
longWriteup:
Situation: College Sauce, a college-focused app, needed to grow its active user base and wanted an incentive structure that turned existing students into a referral-driven acquisition channel.

Task: Design and write a swipeable social carousel that clearly explained a referral leaderboard mechanic — how points were earned, which actions counted, and what winners could win — while keeping the tone playful and native to a college audience.

Action: Structured the carousel around three simple beats: a "How To" panel breaking down point-earning actions (referral signups, joining class group chats, using the app), a "Why" panel laying out a tiered prize ladder from AirPods down to $25 gift cards, and a clear call-to-action with a fixed deadline (winners announced June 14th) to create urgency.

Result: Delivered a self-contained, ready-to-post growth campaign that condensed a multi-step referral program into an easy, scroll-friendly format, giving College Sauce a launch-ready asset tied to a defined contest window.

title: Instagram Ad Targeting: College Freshmen
goal: Convert incoming UCSB freshmen into app downloads by making College Sauce feel like the insider way to find friends, chats, and events during welcome week.
description: Scroll-stopping Instagram ad recruiting UCSB freshmen to a student-built campus community app.
longWriteup:
College Sauce is a social app built by and for UC Santa Barbara students, helping Gauchos find friends, join group chats, and discover events around Isla Vista. The challenge was reaching incoming freshmen in the narrow window before their social habits and app choices settle in during the first weeks of school.

The task was to design a single Instagram ad that could stop the scroll, communicate the app's core value props at a glance, and drive a low-friction download action, all while feeling native to the platform rather than like a corporate pitch.

I built the creative around a Y2K scrapbook aesthetic: disposable-camera-style photos of real UCSB social moments layered over a moody gradient background, paired with bold display type and a phone mockup calling out the app's actual features (Tags, Chats, Live Map). Copy leaned into campus-specific language ("UCSB's hottest app," "Made by Gauchos, for Gauchos") and a UCSB-email requirement to signal exclusivity and build trust with a skeptical, ad-fatigued freshman audience.

The result was a creative that reads as peer-made rather than advertiser-made, using authenticity and local specificity, not production polish, to earn attention and drive downloads.

title: Class of 2024 Seniors Congrats Post
goal: Create a scroll-stopping, on-brand Instagram post congratulating the graduating Class of 2024 to drive engagement and community goodwill.
description: Instagram graphic celebrating the 2024 senior class for College Sauce's social feed.
longWriteup:
College Sauce needed timely, celebratory social content to mark a key seasonal moment for its audience: high school and college seniors graduating in 2024.

The brief was to design and write a single Instagram post that felt celebratory and on-brand, could be understood at a glance in-feed, and encouraged shares and comments from the graduating class and their peers.

I wrote the on-image copy and caption, keeping the message short and celebratory so it would read instantly in a crowded feed, and paired it with a design treatment consistent with College Sauce's existing visual identity.

The post published as part of College Sauce's regular seasonal content cadence, reinforcing the brand's presence around a moment its audience cared about.

title: Exclusive Deals Post
goal: Drive student traffic to local partner businesses by packaging their deals into one shareable, on-brand social post.
description: Social graphic promoting exclusive student discounts at local restaurants and bars via College Sauce.
longWriteup:
College Sauce is a student-focused platform that aggregates discounts from restaurants and bars near campus. The challenge was to turn a rotating list of unrelated deals — from a taco shop's free agua fresca to a liquor store's beer special — into a single piece of content that felt cohesive and worth sharing.

I wrote and designed the post copy so each deal read like a quick, scannable hook (price point or freebie up front, business name attached), then grouped the full roster of partner spots underneath with a clear call to action driving students back to the College Sauce platform for more.

The result was a repeatable content format: a single post that cross-promoted multiple local business partners at once, reinforced College Sauce's value proposition (exclusive, local, student-priced deals), and gave partner businesses added visibility in exchange for their discount listings.

title: App Download CTA Flyer
goal: Convert flyer viewers into College Sauce app downloads by pairing a clear value proposition with a direct call to action.
description: Single-page flyer driving app downloads with a clear, benefit-led call to action.
longWriteup:
College Sauce needed a lightweight, standalone asset to promote its app in settings where a full campaign wasn't practical — tabling events, dorm bulletin boards, social shares, and partner cross-promotion. The flyer had to work as a single visual unit, communicating the app's value and prompting a download without any surrounding context or copy.

I designed the piece around a single hierarchy: one headline benefit, one visual anchor, and one unmistakable call to action. Layout, type scale, and color were chosen to read clearly at both screen size and print size, since the asset needed to double as a physical handout and a digital share graphic.

The result is a flexible CTA flyer that College Sauce could deploy across channels without redesign — proof of being able to distill a product's value into a single scannable visual and pair it with a direct conversion prompt.

title: New Story Feature IG Post
goal: Introduce the new Story feature to College Sauce's audience and prompt users to try it in the app.
description: Instagram post announcing College Sauce's new Story feature to drive awareness and engagement
longWriteup:
Task: Turn that feature list into a single, scannable Instagram post that would read clearly at thumbnail size, feel consistent with the app's visual identity, and give followers a reason to open the app and explore the new categories.

Action: Grouped the six categories into an icon-led layout for fast scanning, wrote tight on-brand copy for each label, and set the visual hierarchy so the "new features" headline read first and the category list supported it.

Result: Delivered a launch-ready IG asset that clearly communicated the expanded category set to the app's audience, giving the team a ready-to-post announcement for the feature rollout.

title: New Categories IG Post
goal: Announce the app's newly added deal categories in a single scroll-stopping Instagram post that stayed on-brand and pointed users back into the app.
description: Instagram graphic announcing six new deal categories added to the CS app, from concept to final asset.
longWriteup:
Situation: CS expanded its in-app marketplace with six new categories — Party, Deals & Discounts, Freebies, Wellness & Self-care, Fundraising & Volunteering, Festivals & Pop-Ups, and Sporting Clubs — but the update hadn't been announced to the brand's Instagram following.

Task: Turn that feature list into a single, scannable Instagram post that would read clearly at thumbnail size, feel consistent with the app's visual identity, and give followers a reason to open the app and explore the new categories.

Action: Grouped the six categories into an icon-led layout for fast scanning, wrote tight on-brand copy for each label, and set the visual hierarchy so the "new features" headline read first and the category list supported it.

Result: Delivered a launch-ready IG asset that clearly communicated the expanded category set to the app's audience, giving the team a ready-to-post announcement for the feature rollout.

title: Integrated Marketing Communications Plan
goal: Build a full-funnel integrated marketing communications plan that unifies positioning, messaging, and channel strategy behind a single set of brand objectives.
description: Team-built IMC plan aligning brand strategy, messaging, and channel mix into one integrated campaign.
longWriteup:
Situation: A brand needed a cohesive marketing communications plan that could tie together advertising, digital, and promotional efforts currently operating as disconnected tactics rather than one coordinated strategy.

Task: Working as part of a five-person team, I helped translate the brand's positioning and target audience insights into a structured IMC plan covering objectives, messaging strategy, media mix, and budget allocation.

Action: I contributed to audience and competitive analysis, helped define key messaging pillars, and worked on channel selection and sequencing to make sure paid, owned, and earned media reinforced the same narrative instead of working against each other. The team then packaged the strategy into a formal plan document with timeline and budget recommendations.

Result: The finished plan demonstrated how a brand's fragmented marketing activities could be unified under one strategic framework, giving stakeholders a clear, actionable roadmap for integrated campaign execution.
